highlights: Hugging Face now routes Inference Providers language-model requests through OpenRouter; code stays the same, but custom provider API keys no longer work for these models.
vLLM v0.34.0 turns on the extensible KV cache by default and removes Model Runner V1, with several breaking changes to check before upgrading.
Anthropic shortens its vulnerability disclosure window from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues and 45 days for the rest, starting January 1, 2027.

items.title: Hugging Face routes language-model inference through OpenRouter
items.summary: Language-model requests on Hugging Face Inference Providers now go through OpenRouter, which routes each request across 80+ providers based on live measurements and retries a failed try on the next best provider inside the same call; Hugging Face adds no markup. You can still pin a policy or provider with a suffix such as :fastest or :cheapest, but you can no longer use your own provider API key for these models, while image, video, and audio generation work as before. Code calling open-weight models with an HF token keeps working; teams relying on their own provider keys should review their setup.

evidence.quote: OpenRouter serves those models at scale, routing each request across 80+ providers based on live measurements of each one.
a failed try is retried on the next best provider inside the same call.
Hugging Face doesn't add a markup on top of it.

You can still choose a policy or a provider with a suffix on the model id: zai-org/GLM-5.3 # default: best mix of price, speed and reliability zai-org/GLM-5.3:fastest # highest throughput zai-org/GLM-5.3:cheapest # lowest price
so you can no longer use your own API key for a provider with these models.
Image, video, and audio generation continue to work exactly as before, directly through Hugging Face Inference Providers without going through OpenRouter.

items.title: vLLM v0.34.0 enables the extensible KV cache by default and drops Model Runner V1
items.summary: vLLM v0.34.0 adds 10 new models (including Mistral Large 4, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash and Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe), sizes the KV cache from memory actually free after warmup by default, and makes Model Runner V2 the only GPU runner, with up to 1.95× decode on Blackwell and MI355X. Breaking changes include a default --block-size of 64 (was 16), gpu memory utilization defaulting to 1.0, dropped ROCm 7.2 images, and a huggingface hub 2.0.0 requirement. Production deployments should go through the upgrade table before bumping the version.

items.title: Anthropic cuts its vulnerability disclosure window from 90 days to 30 and 45
items.summary: Anthropic's coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy moves from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues and 45 days for all others, for vulnerabilities reported on or after January 1, 2027; it will also escalate to an external coordinator after 15 days instead of 30 without a maintainer response, and share full technical details 30 days instead of 45 after a patch. Anthropic says existing norms were developed before AI could discover vulnerabilities and assumed fixes moved at human speed. Vendors and maintainers receiving its reports should plan for faster fixes.

evidence.quote: in our coordinated vulnerability disclosure (CVD) policy from 90 days to 30 days for high- and critical-severity issues, and to 45 days for all other issues. The new timelines apply to vulnerabilities reported to vendors and maintainers on or after January 1, 2027.

First, we will aim to escalate to an external vulnerability coordinator after 15 days instead of 30 if a maintainer does not respond to our initial vulnerability report. Second, we will wait 30 days instead of 45 after a patch is available before sharing full technical details.
Many coordinated disclosure norms, including those found in our own policy, were developed well before AI could discover vulnerabilities. These policies assumed that fixes moved at human speed

items.title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron-Labs-Sigma 8B/3B continuous diffusion language models
items.summary: Nemotron-Labs-Sigma-8B-instruct is an 8-billion-parameter continuous diffusion language model that denoises Gaussian noise in a 16-D continuous token-embedding space instead of generating one token at a time; a 3B variant is also listed. NVIDIA measures roughly 120-140 tokens/s for 256 generated tokens on a single H100 with the DDPM sampler at 32 denoising steps per 64-token block; context is limited to 8,192 tokens, English only, under the NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License. It is a ready-made testbed for anyone exploring parallel diffusion decoding.

evidence.quote: Nemotron-Labs-Sigma-8B-instruct is a 8-billion-parameter continuous diffusion language model. Instead of generating text one token at a time, it denoises Gaussian noise in a low-dimensional (16-D) continuous token-embedding space
Measured generation throughput: roughly 120-140 tokens/s for 256 generated tokens with the DDPM sampler at 32 denoising steps per 64-token block on a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 (bfloat16).
Maximum context length of 8,192 tokens (prompt plus generated tokens). Conversations should be formatted with the bundled chat template (chat_template.jinja). Supported language: English.
Use of this model is governed by the NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License

items.title: Shanghai AI Laboratory releases Sage S2.1 Flash scientific multimodal model
items.summary: Sage S2.1 Flash from Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory targets multi-round scientific research tasks, combining scientific data understanding with retrieval, programming and tool use, and accepts more than ten scientific input types such as molecular graphs, crystal structures and protein structures. The 321B-parameter model ships its code and weights under the MIT License and scores 90.3 on MLE-bench Lite, ahead of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at 89.2. Teams building research or ML-engineering agents get another self-hostable open-weight option.

evidence.quote: The code and model weights in this repository are released under the MIT License
Model size 321B params
Sage S2.1 Flash placed first on MLE-bench Lite with 90.3, ahead of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 at 89.2.

items.title: Liquid AI launches d1.2 and d1.2-ultra decision models with audio input
items.summary: Liquid AI's d1.2 and d1.2-ultra decision models add audio input and five new tasks, such as reading a value from the input, and d1.2-ultra scores 75 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1, two points ahead of the previous best decision model. Both are available on the Liquid API and bill input tokens only, at $0.02 for d1.2 and $0.042 per million input tokens for d1.2-ultra. Developers running classification or extraction calls that need calibrated probabilities can compare them against general-purpose LLMs on cost.

evidence.quote: Today, we release d1.2 and d1.2-ultra, the new versions of our decision models, now supporting audio input and five new tasks. In addition, d1.2-ultra ranks first among decision models on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1.

Both models are available today on the Liquid API , at $0.02 for d1.2 and $0.042 per million input tokens for d1.2-ultra. d1.2 and d1.2-ultra add five new tasks to the API: Read a value from the input (text, number or date).
d1.2-ultra scores 75, the highest on the index and two points ahead of the previous best decision model.
Both models bill input tokens only.

items.title: miHoYo introduces Gamer, a generalist game-playing VLA model
items.summary: Gamer, from the miHoYo Honkai AI R&D team, is a Vision-Language-Action foundation model for long-horizon, real-time game interaction, continually pre-trained on tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction, then trained with sparse-thinking instruction tuning and multi-turn reinforcement learning, and served by the Streaming-vLLM inference engine. The paper reports operational efficiency comparable to skilled players across multiple 3D open-world games and competitive results on 2D game benchmarks. It is a useful reference for anyone scaling GUI or game agents on raw input trajectories.

evidence.quote: We first continue pre-training on a dataset constructed from tens of thousands of hours of device-level keyboard and mouse interaction.
trained through continued pre-training, sparse-thinking instruction tuning, and multi-turn reinforcement learning to interact efficiently in 2D and 3D environments.

Across multiple challenging 3D open-world games, Gamer demonstrates solid generalization and operational efficiency comparable to skilled players. It also achieves competitive results on a range of conventional 2D game benchmarks.
a generalist Vision-Language-Action foundation model for long-horizon, real-time game interaction, developed by the miHoYo Honkai AI R&D team
We develop Streaming-vLLM , a high-concurrency inference engine optimized for continuous game interaction.

items.title: MIRIX-2.0 multi-agent memory system leads LongMemEval-S by 14.3 points
items.summary: MIRIX-2.0 is a multi-agent memory system for LLM agents that is the most accurate of the compared systems on four of five QA benchmarks, reaching 91.4% on LoCoMo and 72.6% on LongMemEval-S, 14.3 points above the strongest baseline. It needs no fine-tuning, runs with closed and open models, and its code is public. Worth adding to the shortlist if you are giving agents long-term memory.

evidence.quote: It is the most accurate of the compared systems on four of five QA benchmarks. It reaches 91.4% on LoCoMo and 72.6% on LongMemEval-S, where it leads the strongest baseline by 14.3 points
It needs no fine-tuning , runs with closed and open models , and its code is public.

items.title: MMFlash speeds up vision-language model decoding by up to 3.58×
items.summary: The authors find drafter acceptance rates fall from 46% in the lowest visual-dependence quartile to 22% in the highest, so MMFlash upweights visually dependent tokens during training and uses sparse attention for long video. Across multimodal benchmarks it reaches lossless decoding speedups of up to 3.58×, outperforming EAGLE-3 and DFlash by up to 195.4% and 17.1%. Teams serving vision-language models should watch drafters built specifically for multimodal inputs.

evidence.quote: We find that acceptance rates decrease from 46% in the lowest visual-dependence quartile to 22% in the highest, with this disparity persisting after multimodal training.
MMFlash improves multimodal speculative decoding by adaptively upweighting visually dependent tokens and using sparse attention for long video, yielding up to 3.58× lossless speedup.
MMFlash achieves lossless decoding speedups of up to 3.58times, outperforming EAGLE-3 and DFlash by up to 195.4% and 17.1%, respectively.

items.title: WebArena-Pro benchmarks web agents on audio and video tasks
items.summary: WebArena-Pro covers 20 self-hosted applications across six domains with 300 human-validated tasks spanning text, vision, audio, and video, and isolates each task for reproducible, parallel evaluation. It supports harness integrations including BrowserGym and Harbor for running MCP and coding agents. Browser-agent builders get a way to test tasks that involve embedded media.

evidence.quote: We're releasing WebArena-Pro, a benchmark for web agents covering 20 self-hosted applications across six domains, with 300 human-validated tasks spanning text, vision, audio, and video, and isolated task execution for reproducible, parallel evaluation.
The benchmark supports multiple harness integrations, including BrowserGym and Harbor for running MCP and coding agents.

items.title: Microsoft Research open-sources TokenEconomizer to cut coding-agent costs
items.summary: TokenEconomizer, an open-source plugin from UC Berkeley, Microsoft Research, and Microsoft Security, learns from past sessions in a repository without changing the agent or model, using one-line micro-skills, tool pruning and failure-loop intervention. On SWE-Bench it lowered mean cost per task by 18.4–30.9% across five agent–model combinations, while Pass@1 rose in four of them. Developers who run agents like Claude Code in the same codebase every day can try it as a drop-in.

evidence.quote: TokenEconomizer, an open-source plugin from UC Berkeley, Microsoft Research, and Microsoft Security, turns completed sessions into guidance for subsequent ones.
Micro-skills capture repository-specific knowledge in one-line notes.
Micro-skills add learned facts, tool pruning trims the loaded tools, and failure-loop intervention redirects stuck work.
On SWE-Bench, TokenEconomizer lowered mean cost per task by 18.4–30.9% across five agent–model combinations (left), while Pass@1 rose in four of them (right).
We first profiled Claude Code on 60 tasks from SWE-Bench

items.title: Coral is an open-source gateway where agents write TypeScript to call tools
items.summary: Coral is an open-source, self-hosted gateway between agents and the systems they work on: agents call tools by writing short TypeScript programs, each run in a fresh V8 isolate with no network access, credentials or imports, and Coral checks every tool call against workspace policy before adding credentials. Programs that work can be saved as custom tools to reuse, and the core is under the Apache License 2.0. Teams connecting agents to internal systems with tight permissions should take a look.

evidence.quote: Coral is an open-source, self-hosted gateway that sits between your agents and the systems they work on. Agents call tools by writing short TypeScript programs, and save the ones that work as custom tools to reuse.

Each program runs in a fresh V8 isolate with no network access, no credentials, and no imports. Coral checks every tool call against your workspace policy, then adds the credentials and forwards the call to the provider.
Coral is licensed under the Apache License 2.0.

items.title: Tencent announces Hy4 flash with 224B total and 12B active parameters
items.summary: Tencent calls Hy4 flash its most cost-effective Hy model to date, with 224B total parameters (including 64B Engram parameters), 12B active per token, native multimodality, a 1M-token context window and significantly lower API pricing.

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.326 allows Code Mode with agent teams enabled
items.summary: Claude Code v2.1.326 lets you turn on Code Mode while agent teams are enabled and warns at startup when an --allowedTools, --disallowedTools or --tools entry doesn't look like a complete rule.

items.title: OpenAI begins its first phase of embedded safety assessments
items.summary: OpenAI signed agreements with Apollo Research, METR, Transluce, and Goodfire to give independent experts deep, extended access to its internal models and systems to assess alignment and the effectiveness of safeguards.

evidence.quote: We have signed agreements with four independent assessors—Apollo Research, METR, Transluce, and Goodfire—for our first phase of embedded assessments.
Embedded assessments give independent experts deep access to a lab’s internal models and systems to assess model alignment and the effectiveness of safeguards over an extended period of time

items.title: Cohere adds Video Intelligence to Compass
items.summary: Cohere's Video Intelligence in Compass searches what's said and shown in video libraries, returns timestamped clips with transcripts and visual descriptions, connects to agents via the Compass MCP server, and is recruiting design partners.

evidence.quote: Compass understands both what's said and what's shown on screen. Instead of returning an hour-long recording, it retrieves the exact moment that answers a question, with a timestamped clip, transcript and visual description. We're now recruiting design partners.
Connect your agent to the Compass MCP server so it can reason over what's shown on screen

items.title: Analysis finds Windows 11 records which coding agents you use
items.summary: A reverse-engineering write-up found MissionControlAggregator.dll on the author's Windows 11 machine recording which coding agents and developer tools were used, queued for upload to Microsoft when optional diagnostic data is allowed.

evidence.quote: I checked my Parallels Windows 11 ARM64 VM, build 26200.9974 . Its MissionControlAggregator.dll was version 10.0.26100.9818 , and CLICodingAgentUsage was already enabled as a service experiment.
When optional diagnostic data is allowed (enabled by default in the US setup I tested), Windows queues the coding-agent usage report for upload to Microsoft.

items.title: Gemma 4 tokenizer patch fixes 219 glitch tokens
items.summary: google/gemma-4-E4B-it merged a tokenizer-only patch that remediates 219 glitch tokens causing unpredictable model behavior, with no weights modified; a community post says E2B and 12B got the same fix.

evidence.quote: This PR patches tokenizer.json to remediate 219 glitch tokens identified by embedding vector analysis. Glitch tokens are vocabulary entries whose embeddings have collapsed to near-identical representations, causing unpredictable model behavior when they appear in input. No model weights are modified
